result.title: Counterfactual Certification for Sequential Unlearning with Long-Run Performance Guarantees
result.summary: Certified machine unlearning ensures the proximity between the unlearned model and a model retrained without the data to be forgotten. Extending this framework to sequential deletion requests, typically arriving as groups of variable size (e.g., all records of one user or of coordinated users), is challenging. For unlearning methods based on fine-tuning on the retain sets, this leads to either degrading performance or increasing computation as the number of unlearning requests grows. For independent successive requests, we instead certify each model release against a counterfactual unlearning trajectory in which the group being deleted never took part. With a fixed fine-tuning budget per deletion, we show that, for smooth strongly convex objectives, this approach keeps the performance loss bounded, uniformly in the number of requests. Experiments with multiclass logistic regression on FEMNIST show that the resulting algorithm needs fewer corrective steps than existing sequential methods and outperforms training-time differential privacy, particularly when group sizes are heterogeneous.

AI.brief_summary: 研究序列式机器遗忘的反事实认证问题：针对按组到达的删除请求，用固定微调预算对每次模型发布给出相对「该组从未参与」的反事实轨迹的认证，并在强凸目标下界定理性能损失，在 FEMNIST 逻辑回归上验证。
